framework.52w_position_analysis: Price at ₹139 sits 46% below the 52w high of ₹258 and 30% above the 52w low of ₹107. This is not a technical breakout story — it is closer to the floor than the ceiling. The drawdown was driven by FY26 profit compression, not business failure. The stock is in recovery mode but valuation remains elevated.
framework.revenue_trend_yoy: Revenue growing consistently: FY24 ₹63 Cr → FY25 ₹78 Cr (+23%) → FY26 ₹92 Cr (+18%). The 3-year CAGR of 18% shows deceleration from the 10-year CAGR of 39%, which is expected as the base grows. The absolute trajectory is intact and the Q4FY26 run-rate of ₹27 Cr per quarter implies FY27 revenue of ₹100+ Cr at current pace.
framework.cheap_or_ignored: The stock is ignored + suffering a capex digestion phase. Business fundamentals are solid — revenue and operating profit both grew in FY26 (EBITDA +20%). The PAT decline (-17%) is entirely explained by: (1) depreciation nearly doubling from ₹1.81 Cr to ₹3.88 Cr as the large CWIP (₹32.52 Cr in FY25) was commissioned into fixed assets; (2) interest cost rising ₹1.36 Cr → ₹2.59 Cr on capex debt; (3) effective tax rate spiking to 40.5% from 30.5% (likely deferred tax adjustment on accelerated depreciation). The business is not deteriorating — it is absorbing a capacity expansion.
framework.promoter_open_market_buying: Promoter holding has been rock-solid at 73.06–73.07% across all 12 quarters shown (Sep 2023 – Jun 2026). There is no evidence of open-market buying. The stability signals confidence but the absence of incremental buying means there is no insider-conviction catalyst here.
framework.growing_business_at_fair_price: The business quality is high: OPM expanded from 4% (FY16) to 19%+ (FY26) over a decade — a strong operational leverage story. Debtor days improved from 84 to 28. FCF turned decisively positive in FY25 (₹0.64 Cr) and FY26 (₹5.76 Cr) after years of capex burn. However, at P/E 42.3x on depressed FY26 earnings (with a high tax anomaly), the price is not cheap. If FY27 earnings normalize — assuming depreciation stabilizes, interest cost is absorbed by higher revenue, and tax rate reverts to ~27% — PAT could recover to ₹9–10 Cr, implying a forward P/E of 29–32x. That is still not bargain-priced for 18% revenue growth.
framework.peg_analysis: Using 3-year revenue CAGR of 18% as the growth proxy, PEG = 42.3 / 18 = 2.35 — above the 2.0 threshold for fair value. Using 3-year profit CAGR of 8%, PEG = 5.3 — expensive. The PEG is misleading in isolation here because profits are temporarily suppressed; the true economic EBITDA growth (EBITDA +20% YoY) supports a better picture. But on reported earnings, the stock is priced for perfection.
framework.relative_valuation_vs_peers: Elevator sector peers (Kone India, TK Elevator, Johnson Lifts — unlisted; listed peers like Otis India at much larger scale) are hard to compare directly. In the small/micro-cap elevator component space, a 17–20x EV/EBITDA is common for companies with 18–25% growth. Aaron's EV/EBITDA (approx. 17–18x based on FY26 EBITDA of ₹17.79 Cr and EV ~₹318 Cr) is at the upper end but not absurd for the growth trajectory. However, the profit multiple (42x PE) is the visible number that keeps institutional buyers away.

key_risks: FY26 profit declined (-17%) despite revenue growth — market legitimately spooked
Tax rate anomaly at 40.5% needs management clarification (Q1FY27 concall Aug 17 will help)
High cash conversion cycle (~136 days) — working capital intensive business
Debt increased to fund capex; interest will remain elevated until revenue scales
Small cap with limited liquidity; 73% promoter holding leaves only 27% float
Real estate cycle dependency — elevator demand linked to construction activity
No institutional following; analyst coverage absent
key_catalysts: New manufacturing capacity fully commissioned — FY27 should see revenue acceleration
Q4FY26 run-rate (₹27.33 Cr revenue, ₹2.32 Cr PAT) is the strongest ever — trajectory improving
Q1FY27 concall (Aug 17, 2026) could clarify tax anomaly and provide guidance
New EVOQ360 distributor appointment (Aug 11 announcement) signals product expansion
OPM at 19–21% and expanding — above-average for manufacturing
FCF positive and improving — quality of earnings getting better
If PAT recovers to ₹9–10 Cr in FY27, forward P/E drops to 29–32x — more justifiable
quarterly_recovery_signal: Strong sequential profit improvement in FY26: Q1 ₹1.06 Cr → Q2 ₹1.39 Cr → Q3 ₹2.02 Cr → Q4 ₹2.32 Cr. This J-curve matches the capex commissioning hypothesis — the new plant ramped during FY26 and earnings are clearly recovering. This is the most bullish signal in the dataset.
reasoning: Aaron Industries is a real, growing business that has compounded revenue at 39% over 10 years and expanded OPM from 4% to 19%. The FY26 profit decline is a textbook capex digestion effect — the company commissioned a major plant expansion (CWIP of ₹32 Cr became ₹55 Cr in fixed assets), causing depreciation and interest to spike. This temporarily crushed reported profits while operating profit actually grew. The market sold off 46% from the high, which is an overreaction to a transient earnings dip. However, calling this a PASS would require the stock to be cheap. It is not. At P/E 42x on depressed earnings and PEG 2.35x on revenue growth, the valuation demands flawless execution. The promoter has not signaled conviction through buying. The real test is FY27: if Q1FY27 results (just released Aug 11, concall Aug 17) show PAT recovering above ₹2 Cr per quarter with tax rates normalizing, this becomes a PASS. On current information — elevated P/E, declining TTM profits, no promoter buying, but intact revenue growth and clear recovery trajectory — the verdict is BORDERLINE. Worth monitoring closely post-Q1FY27 concall. Entry would be more compelling below ₹110–120 where PEG approaches 1.5x and the margin of safety improves.
